strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to; a) analyse priced 2 Dimension and 3 Dimension artworks to conceptualize factors considered in costing of artwork, b) calculate the unit cost artworks for proper value placement, c) explore factors that influence a consumer’s purchasing decisions, and designs a 3-colour chart, d) appreciate the importance of consumer’s purchasing decisions in artwork.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to; ● study actual and virtual priced 2 Dimension and 3 Dimension artworks to consider factors used in costing artwork; - hourly wage - time taken in production -cost of materials -Overhead costs - commission - Market price ● calculate the cost of artwork using given formulae that considers the following 5 aspects: (reasonable daily wage x number of days used to produce the artwork + the cost of materials used + overhead costs + profit margin at 30% of cost of material)
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can an artist determine the price of an artwork? 2. Why is a consumer’s purchasing behaviour important when marketing Artworks?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to; a) analyse components of perspective in sample cuboids drawn in two - point perspective, b) draw cuboids in two point perspective from different views, c) draw buildings in two- point perspective and shade using cross hatching technique, d) appreciate own and other is two-point perspective drawings.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to; • observe and discuss actual or virtual cuboids drawn in two-point perspective and identify the components of perspective: - projection lines /convergence lines (orthogonal lines) - Two vanishing points - horizon • draw cuboids in two - point perspective and explore; - normal eye view - bird’s eye view - worms’ eye view with emphasis on; - projection lines/convergence lines - vanishing point - horizon • draw buildings in two point perspective based on normal view and shade by cross hatching with emphasis on,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you create a 2-point linear perspective drawing on cuboid? 2. How does perspective affect the illusion of objects?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to:- a) analyse warm and cool colours on the colour wheel and sample paintings in regard to colour temperature, b) create an imaginative seascape composition based on colour temperature, c) investigate the psychological, cultural and conventional symbolic meaning of colours, d) appreciate the use of colour temperature and symbolic
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to; • identify and discuss warm and cool colours as represented on the actual or virtual colour wheel in regards to; - Receding/advancing colours • observe and discuss sample paintings in regards to the use of warm and cool colours to create recession and projection of spaces and objects • paint an imaginative pictorial composition of a seascape with focus on either warm or cool colours - seascape (cool or warm colours)
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. What effect can colour temperature have in a pictorial composition? 2. What emotions do different colours evoke in us when we look at them?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to:- a) analyse characteristics of mosaic from sample artworks, b) identify functions of mosaic art in contemporary society, c) create a paper mosaic landscape pictorial composition for self- expression, d) create an egg shell mosaic landscape pictorial composition of a flower for self- expression, e) appreciate own and others’ pictorial composition.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to; • observe virtual or actual samples to analyse the characteristics of mosaic; - variety of materials used in making tesserae (egg shells, paper, leaves, fabric, pebbles, tiles, glass etc.) - narrow spacing between tesserae - tonal variation of tesserae • discuss functions of mosaic art in contemporary society; - interior decoration - decorative arts ● collaboratively collect re-usable papers, eggshells to be used in creating mosaic while observing safety measures ● individually create a mosaic composition of a landscape with emphasis on- -sorting of coloured papers -cutting the paper into tesserae -pasting while observing appropriate spacing and tonal variation of tesserae
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you determine appropriate materials and tools for mosaic? 2. Why is the spacing of the tesserae important in mosaic?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) study features of flip books with two moving objects against a painted background, b) make flip book of two moving objects against a painted background, c) manipulate the flip book to animate the moving objects, d) appreciate own and others’ flip book animations.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to: • observe and discuss actual or virtual flip books having two moving objects against a painted background with emphasis on: - materials and tools used - Sequencing of images (Positioning of objects on subsequent pages). - frequency of images (speed of flick per second). • prepare the flip book using the following procedure; - collating the papers - trimming the papers - creation of a painted background using wash technique - creation of sequence of two moving objects with focus on; creativity (storyline), o
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is the wash technique ideal for creating a background for a flip book? 2. What role do flipbooks play in the society?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse logo design samples for conceptualisation, b) design a logo in two colours for an institution, c) appreciate own and others’ logo designs.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to; • Explore and discuss logo design samples from virtual or actual sources(e.g. magazines, newspapers etc.) with focus on: - Its use as a legal identification symbol (NGOs, banks, parastatal, international organizations etc.) - Its characteristics - simple - Relevant - Memorable - Timeless - Versatile - Its components (Letter, word, image or combination of either) -Where it is applied ( products, stationary, advertisements) • design a logo in two contrasting colours for an imaginary company in freehand, taking into account the following;
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you make a logo interesting? 2. why should one consider the style of lettering when designing a logo

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse samples of trademark designs for conceptualisation, b) design a trademark in two colours for a company, c) appreciate own and others’ trademark designs.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to; • analyse and discuss trademark design samples from virtual or actual sources with focus on; - Its use as a legal identification symbol (commercial companies, production industries) -Where it is applied (products, advertisements) - characteristics, (word, image or combination of word and image) • design a trademark in two colours for a company using freehand • design a trademark in two colours for a company using digital devices guided by the same instructions given
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is a trademark important for a business? 2. What steps are followed in the creation of a trademark?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse sample objects ornamented using yarn, b) decorate found objects using yarn for self-expression, c) appreciate own and others’ decorated objects decorated using yarn.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to: ● Observe an actual demonstration or watch a video clip on ornamentation of objects using yarns and identify; - Found objects that can be decorated - Types of yarn used - Method of securing yarn ● collect and prepare used yarn from the environment while observing safety measures with focus on: - unravelling the yarn old articles - washing and drying the yarn - spooling the yarn • collect found objects and clean them while observing hygiene measures • create decorations on found objects ( bottles, containers) using the yarn with focus on :
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you secure the ends of the yarn during the decorative process? 2. Why should reused yarn and objects be cleaned before usage?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse sample objects ornamented made using paper craft techniques, b) create decorations on found objects using paper craft techniques for self-expression, c) appreciate own and others’ paper decorated objects.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to: • watch a video or actual demonstration on ornamentation of objects using paper craft to identify; - paper craft techniques used - types of objects that can be decorated - types of paper that can be used - finishing of the work -types of adhesives used vs the surfaces • collect and sort used paper from the environment while observing hygiene measures with focus on; -texture of paper - colour of paper -weight of paper - paper finish (e.g. glossy/shiny etc. • collect and clean appropriate objects from the environment while observing safety measures • explore the paper craft techniques
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you secure the ends of the yarn during the decorative process? 2. Why is it important to recycle or reuse found objects for ornamentation?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse samples of sculptural forms made by assemblage and construction , b) assemble and construct a sculpture by reusing materials for self- expression, c) appreciate own and others’ assemblage and construction sculptural forms.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to: • observe and discuss sculptural forms made by assemblage and construction from actual or virtual sources to identify; - reuse of materials (wires, wood, sheet metal, paper, plastics, fabric, rubber, buttons, hairs, fibre etc. ) -weight of materials -size and display space -joining techniques • sketch the human or animal form • collect, sort and prepare the materials (cleaning, trimming, cutting to size) • assemble and construct a human or animal figure from assorted locally available materials while
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is the choice of material important in construction and assemblage of sculptural forms? 2. How would you determine the best way of joining different parts of constructed and assembled sculpture?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse the elements and principles of 3 Dimensional modelled sculptures, b) create clay modelled sculptural forms for self-expression, c) appreciate own and others’ modelled sculptures.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to: • observe, identify and discuss elements and principles of 3- Dimensional art in actual or virtual samples of modelled sculptures; Elements: - Space: - Line: - Plane - Mass/volume: - Shape: - Value: - Texture: - Colour Principles: - Unity/harmony: - Contrast/variety rhythm/ repetition - Emphasis: - Balance: - Proportion/scale:
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why do we need to use an armature when modelling sculpture in the round? 2. What can you do to prevent modelled sculptures from cracking?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse samples of one-piece mould casting to familiarise with the concept, b) cast sculptural forms using one piece mould for skill development, c) appreciate own and others’ cast sculptures.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to: ● watch actual or virtual demonstration of one-piece mould casting and discuss the process and the materials and tools used. ● collaboratively; - source materials and tools required (papers, glue, cutting tools, mixing containers) - select a simple one-piece mould (bowl, plate or saucer etc) - prepare clay or papier maché for casting - cast forms using the outer part of the one-piece mould while paying attention to; - size and thickness of the walls - finishing techniques - display and critique own and others’ cast sculptures.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you prevent clay or papier maché from sticking on to the mould? 2. Why is casting technique important as an artwork production method?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse characteristics of sample functional slab vessels, b) model a functional vessel using slab technique, c) decorate the vessel using a combination of techniques, d) fire the modelled vessels in the down draught kiln,. e) critique own and others’ fired slab vessels.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to : ● study characteristics of actual or virtual samples of functional slab vessels with focus on; -shape -dimensions -thickness of walls -decoration • model a vessel using slab technique, - preparation of clay - preparation of slab -partial drying of slabs - preparation of slip -joining of slabs - drying of vessels • decorate the vessel using any of techniques - embedding - slip trailing - inlaying - burnishing
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can you enhance the beauty of the modelled vessel? 2. What can you do to ensure that the vessel you have made does not crack during the drying and firing processes?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse a demonstration on pellet technique to acquaint with the process, b) model a functional vessel using pellet technique, c) decorate the modelled vessel using different techniques, d) build a down draught kiln in readiness for firing, e) fire the modelled vessels in the down draught kiln, f) appraise own and others’ fired vessels.
strands.experiences: Learner is guided to : • study and discuss an actual demonstration or video on pellet technique focusing on;- - size of the ball, - even pressing of the wall/pinching - smoothing/finishing • model a vessel using pellet technique - preparation of clay - making of pellets - joining pellets (moist to moist and slip method) - smoothening - drying • decorate the modelled vessel using different techniques (embedding, slip trailing, inlaying).
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. What is the importance of firing clay vessels? 2. Why do we need to embellish clay vessels?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse samples of pile weave structure to understand the concept, b) make a frame loom using mitre joints to be used in pile weaving, c) create a two colour wall hanging using pile weave for self-expression, d) apply finishing techniques on the wall hanging, e) appreciate own and others’ woven artwork.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: • analyse virtual or and actual samples of 2/2 twill weave on: - materials and tools used - weaving device (frame loom) • make a frame loom using mitre joints to be used in weaving with emphasis on: - alignment of joints - sturdiness of the frame - nail spacing - observe safety precautions while handling materials and tools • Select and reuse flexible weaving materials available in the locality, namely; - - woollen yarn - Plain coloured cloth • warp the loom in pairs, with emphasis on: - equal tension of warps
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is it important to maintain even tension during weaving? 2. How can you finish a woven wall hanging?
